chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Marwan ibn Muslim and Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
The area from the parting of the hair to the tip of the nose is a place of prostration (sajdah); whichever part of that area touches the ground, it suffices for you.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: It suffices for you / It is valid for you
key_terms.قُصَاصِ الشَّعْرِ: The parting or beginning of the hair on the forehead
key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ: A place of prostration (referring to the forehead)

ai.seo_question: What is the valid area of the forehead for prostration in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise anatomical boundaries for valid prostration, specifying the area between the hairline and the tip of the nose as the designated 'place of prayer' (masjid). It establishes a principle of flexibility, indicating that contact with any part of this region suffices for the validity of the ritual, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease and precision in worship. This definition is crucial for distinguishing between the forehead's skin and the hair itself during sujood.
